_meta.confidence: High for the underlying figures (transcribed directly from the district's own report tables) -- but see fiscal_year_mismatch_warning and small_reconciliation_gap below before using alongside the other two districts.
_meta.fiscal_year_mismatch_warning: Central Curry and Brookings-Harbor's data in this project are both FY2025-26 Adopted. This Port Orford-Langlois data is FY2026-27. That's a one-year offset -- state and local revenue figures will reflect a different year's rates and enrollment, so a direct side-by-side dollar comparison across all three districts would be comparing different fiscal years. If the app wants strict comparability, either source Port Orford-Langlois's FY2025-26 figures separately, or clearly label each district's fiscal year in the UI (the existing per-district fiscal_year field already supports this) and avoid implying the three numbers are contemporaneous.
_meta.small_reconciliation_gap: The report's revenue/expenditure-by-OBJECT total ($6,575,069.28) and its expenditure-by-FUNCTION total ($6,549,069.28, from the 'General Fund (100) Appropriations' table) differ by $26,000. This is a small gap in the source document itself (likely a rounding or presentation difference between the two tables in this monthly report, not an error in transcription) -- flagged rather than silently resolved. Use the by-function total ($6,549,069.28) for the Instruction/Support Services/Other breakdown below, and the by-object total ($6,575,069.28) for the revenue-side total, matching how each table is labeled in the source.

budget_message_highlights: No enrollment-decline or funding-pressure narrative was available for this district in this pass -- unlike Central Curry and Brookings-Harbor, this source is a monthly business-office report, not an annual adopted-budget message with that kind of commentary. If a fuller Port Orford-Langlois budget document turns up later, check it for a comparable pull-quote.
District mission statement (from the report header): 'We are here to help our Students... Navigate Challenges with Grace, Prepare for Their Futures and Anchor Themselves in Our Community.'

The district ran a free breakfast and lunch program for ALL children 18 and under (not limited to enrolled students) from June 22 to August 6, 2026, timed to coincide with its summer Ready-Set-Learn, Extended School Year, and Credit Recovery programs -- a concrete example of a small district's community-facing use of federal/state child nutrition funding, worth a mention if the app covers food service programs.

intermediate.note: Same 'intermediate' category pattern seen in Brookings-Harbor's budget -- very small for this district.

federal.note: Budgeted at $0 for FY2026-27, unlike Central Curry ($75,000) and Brookings-Harbor ($1,013,025), both of which budgeted federal forest fee revenue. Worth double-checking against next year's actuals or an earlier fiscal year -- this could reflect real district-specific circumstances (e.g. different federal land holdings in this district's boundary) or simply a conservative $0 budget placeholder pending uncertain federal payments, consistent with the O&C/SRS funding uncertainty already noted in non-property-tax-revenue.json from an earlier pass.

general_fund_expenditures_by_program.note: This total is $26,000 less than the revenue-side total -- see small_reconciliation_gap above.

app_display_guidance.suggested_grouping: Use the same Instruction / Support Services / Other framing as the other two districts for the primary view, using the by-function figures above ($6,549,069.28 total). Note in the UI (or in a footnote) that Port Orford-Langlois's data reflects a different fiscal year (2026-27) than Central Curry and Brookings-Harbor (2025-26) -- don't present all three as if they're the same snapshot in time.
app_display_guidance.biggest_single_program: Support Services ($3,288,451.07) is actually larger than Instruction ($2,980,965.51) for this district -- the opposite pattern from what the object-level detail alone would suggest, and worth double-checking against a fuller budget document if one is found, since it's a notable data point (a small district where support/administrative costs slightly exceed direct instruction costs).
app_display_guidance.scale_note: Port Orford-Langlois's General Fund (~$6.5-6.6M) is the smallest of the three districts -- smaller than Central Curry (~$7.7M) despite Central Curry also being a small district, and much smaller than Brookings-Harbor (~$21.7M). Consistent with it having the smallest enrollment of the three (roughly 220-300 students).
